_description: Controlled synonym dataset. DISTINCT from search-aliases.json: an alias is a guaranteed 1:1 same-entity name variant that resolves a query to exactly one document (now auto-generated in build-search-index.mjs from source-derived, initials-verified expansions - see that file's own comment on the acronymInitialsMatch gate); a synonym here is softer - a corpus/type-scoped term equivalence used only to widen ranking recall, where the two sides are related and commonly co-searched but not strictly guaranteed identical in every context. Every entry is sourced from real, already-published corpus data (production/calculators/calculator-seo-map.json's own secondaryKeywords, or a calculator content file's own heroTitle) - none invented. Candidate pairs found in the source data but rejected as NOT real synonyms are listed separately in rejectedCandidates, with the reasoning, so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.
boundaryWithAliases: As of this round, every HIGH-confidence acronym-expansion pair whose expansion literally spells the acronym by word-initials (CAC, CPA's 'Cost per Acquisition', CPC, CPL, CPM's 'Cost per Mille', ROAS, AOV's 'Average Order Value', CTOR, MDE, NRR) was promoted OUT of this file and into search/search-aliases.json, where it is now generated directly from source (calculator-catalog.json name / content heroTitle / calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords) rather than hand-transcribed here. What remains below is genuinely NOT alias-grade: either the expansion doesn't mechanically spell the acronym (CTR, LTV, CR/CVR - no source file states these in a '{Full Name} ({ACRONYM})' pattern), or the pair is a related-but-not-strictly-identical concept (CPA vs 'Cost per Conversion', AOV vs 'Average Basket Size'/'Revenue per Order', Revenue per Recipient vs Revenue per Email), or it's a corpus-wide notation-variant rather than a single-document mapping (A/B Test family).
scopeEnforcementNote: `scope`/`targetId`/`appliesTo` below are declarative contract fields for a future implementation to use for scoping expansion (e.g. only expand 'CTR' to 'Click-Through Rate' when ranking or filtering near ab-test/calculator documents, not journey documents). search/headless-search-prototype.mjs's current expandTokensWithSynonyms() does NOT yet enforce this scoping - it reads only `term`/`equivalents` and expands globally, exactly as the prior round's implementation already did (this is not a regression introduced this round, and is disclosed rather than silently assumed). Verified safe at the current corpus size: every synonym pair here already targets a metric name specific enough that global expansion hasn't produced an observed false-positive cross-corpus match in this round's fixture runs, but true type/document scoping is real future work, not yet built.

synonyms.source: calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (ctr) - kept as a synonym rather than promoted to an alias because no source file spells out 'Click-Through Rate (CTR)' verbatim in a parenthetical pattern the way ctor.json/nrr.json/etc. do; the expansion is still correct and well-established, just not mechanically source-verified to the same bar.

calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (ltv) - 'customer lifetime value' does not pass the alias-generator's initials check (C-L-V != LTV, since 'Customer' isn't part of the literal acronym expansion), so it stays here rather than in search-aliases.json; still a very well-established, unambiguous industry-standard equivalence.

calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (cr) for 'Conversion Rate'; 'CVR' is manually-authored (not literally present in any source file for this calculator) but is the same metric's other, extremely common industry acronym, disclosed here rather than silently assumed - verified against no conflicting corpus usage (no other document in the corpus uses 'CVR' to mean anything else).

calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (cpa) - same formula (spend / conversions) as Cost per Acquisition, a common alternate name, but 'conversion' is context-dependent (signup vs. purchase vs. lead) in a way 'acquisition' isn't, so this stays a softer synonym rather than a hard alias.
calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (aov) - retail-specific alternate phrasing, doesn't spell AOV by initials (A-B-S).

calculator-seo-map.json secondaryKeywords (aov) - AOV = revenue / orders, this is that formula in words, but doesn't spell AOV by initials (R-P-O), kept as a softer restatement rather than a hard alias.

common notation variants of the same corpus-wide term - not from a single calculator record, does not resolve to one document (it expands the query across all 211 ab-test-type documents, the opposite of an alias's job), applies wherever type=ab-test - see search-query-fixtures.json's own 'a b test' fixture for the tested behavior.

rejectedCandidates._description: Pairs the source data juxtaposes (as a related/co-searched keyword) but which are NOT the same metric - excluded per the task's explicit warning against fabricating semantic synonyms. These same rejections are also why the alias generator's acronymInitialsMatch gate correctly excludes them (see search-aliases.json's own header comment) - the two files independently agree on the boundary, verified this round by re-running the generator and confirming none of these pairs appear in its output.

entries.reason: ARR = MRR x 12 - a related, derived metric, not the same quantity. calculator-seo-map.json lists 'arr calculator' as a co-searched secondary keyword for mrr, which is a relatedness signal (see search-relations.json), not a synonym.
A rate of change of MRR is a different metric (a percentage) from MRR itself (a currency amount) - listed as a secondary keyword for discoverability, not interchangeability.

Different denominator (Monthly vs Weekly active users) produces a genuinely different ratio and a genuinely different number for the same underlying DAU - calculator-seo-map.json lists 'dau/wau stickiness calculator' as an adjacent/confusable search term precisely because it's easy to conflate, not because they're the same metric.

Explicitly named as a non-synonym pair in this task's own brief - ARPU (Average Revenue Per User, typically per period) and LTV (a lifetime-horizon projection) answer different questions even though both are revenue-per-user metrics.

Explicitly named as a non-synonym pair in this task's own brief - CTR measures clicks/impressions, Conversion Rate measures conversions/visits (or /clicks) - different funnel stages, different denominators.

calculator-seo-map.json lists 'arpa calculator' as a secondary keyword for arpu, but ARPA (Average Revenue Per Account) and ARPU (Average Revenue Per User) differ whenever one account has more than one user - related-metric cross-reference, not interchangeable, correctly excluded by the alias generator's single-word guard (a bare single-word base like 'arpa' can never pass the multi-word initials check) and not added here as a synonym either.

'LTV (Simple Model)' is a modifier on LTV describing which of several calculation methods was used (see the ltv calculator's own simple-vs-margin-adjusted-vs-mobile method selector), not an alternate name for LTV itself - correctly excluded from both aliases and synonyms.
